name: Entrepreneurship in Emerging Economies
objectives: For one emerging economy you choose, explain what an emerging economy is and name two opportunities and two challenges there, marking every fact that needs checking
Given your military skills, write a one-sentence business idea that matches one skill to a real local problem, naming the service, customer, place and how they pay

For your business idea, plan market research with AI and check key facts in the official Country Commercial Guide and business registry, answering at least two research questions from official sources
Using your one-sentence idea, write a one-page business model with AI help, with all seven parts and every guess marked "to test"
For your business model, list your start-up costs and your top three risks with one way to reduce each, with prices from real quotes and no plan that relies on a bribe
Before you spend real money, plan a small, cheap pilot of your idea and choose one official help program to contact, with the program named and a date to contact it

lessons.title: Lesson 1: What an emerging economy is
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Explain what an emerging economy is and name two opportunities and two challenges.
This lesson builds toward: For one emerging economy you choose, you will explain what an emerging economy is and name two opportunities and two challenges there, marking every fact that needs checking.
An emerging economy is a country whose economy is growing and changing fast, moving from mostly farming or raw materials toward more industry, services and technology. Examples often named include Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, India, Vietnam, Indonesia and Brazil.
Opportunities: young, growing populations; fast phone and internet growth; mobile money, such as M-Pesa in Kenya, that lets people pay by phone; and real gaps in services such as power, transport, cold storage, training and security.
Challenges: rules that change, slower paperwork, currency swings, weaker roads or power in some areas, and corruption risk. Success depends on local partners, patience and checking the facts on official sources.
Words to know:
- Emerging economy: a country whose economy is growing and changing fast.
- Mobile money: a way to send, receive and store money on a phone, often without a bank account.
- Currency swing: when the value of a country's money rises or falls against other currencies.
Try it now: Pick one emerging economy you know or are curious about. Ask an AI assistant: "In plain words, name three growing needs and three business challenges in [country]." Mark each fact you will need to check.
You can now explain what an emerging economy is and name its opportunities and challenges.

check.q: What makes a country an emerging economy?
options: Its economy is growing and changing fast
It has the same rules as the United States
check.why: Emerging economies grow and change quickly, which brings both opportunities and challenges.

check.q: An AI lists three business challenges in a country you chose. What do you do?
options: Pick a different country right away
Mark each fact you will need to check on an official source
check.why: AI answers about other countries can be wrong or out of date, so you mark facts to check.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Turning military skills into a business idea
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Match one of your military skills to a real local problem and write a one-sentence business idea.
This lesson builds toward: Given your military skills, you will write a one-sentence business idea that matches one skill to a real local problem, naming the service, customer, place and how they pay.
The best ideas solve a real problem people will pay to fix. Start with what you know how to do. Military skills that fit emerging markets well include logistics and supply (moving and storing goods), power and generator maintenance, vehicle and equipment repair, security planning, communications and IT, medical support training, and teaching and training people.
Then match a skill to a problem. Example: a former Army logistics NCO sees that small farmers lose produce before it reaches market. Idea: "A shared cold-storage and pickup service for smallholder farmers near Nakuru, paid per crate by mobile money."
Ask AI to brainstorm, but you choose. Prompt: "I was a Navy electrician for 8 years. List 10 small business ideas in Ghana that use these skills to solve a local problem. One line each." Pick the one you can test cheaply.
Step by step:
- List three military skills you are good at.
- List three real problems in your chosen country.
- Ask AI to brainstorm ideas that match them.
- Pick one idea you could test cheaply.
- Write it as one sentence: service, customer, place, how they pay.
Words to know:
- Business idea: a product or service that solves a problem for a customer who will pay.
- Smallholder farmer: a farmer with a small plot of land, common in many emerging economies.
Try it now: Ask an AI assistant for ten business ideas that use your military skills in your chosen country. Pick one and write it as one sentence: service, customer, place, how they pay.
You can now turn a military skill into a one-sentence business idea that solves a local problem.

check.q: What makes a business idea strong?
options: It solves a real problem people will pay to fix
check.why: A business lasts when it fixes a real problem customers will pay for.

check.q: The AI gives you ten business ideas. What do you do?
options: Choose one that uses your skills and write it as one sentence
Pick the one with the biggest numbers
check.why: You choose the idea that fits your skills and write it clearly: service, customer, place, how they pay.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Researching the market with AI and official guides
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Use AI to plan market research and check key facts in the official Country Commercial Guide.
This lesson builds toward: For your business idea, you will plan market research with AI and check key facts in the official Country Commercial Guide and business registry, answering at least two research questions from official sources.
AI can help you plan research and list questions, but it can be wrong or out of date about foreign markets and laws. Use it to draft; use official sources to check.
The U.S. Department of Commerce's International Trade Administration publishes Country Commercial Guides, prepared by U.S. Embassy staff, covering how a market works, opportunities, rules and business customs. Its U.S. Commercial Service also helps U.S. businesses that sell abroad with market research and contacts.
To start a company in the country itself, find its official business registry. In Kenya it is the Business Registration Service (brs.go.ke); in Nigeria it is the Corporate Affairs Commission (cac.gov.ng). Read their current steps and fees yourself, and talk to five possible customers before you spend real money.
Step by step:
- Ask AI: "What 10 questions should I answer before starting [idea] in [country]?"
- Read the country's Country Commercial Guide on trade.gov.
- Find the country's official business registry and read its current steps.
- Talk to five possible customers about the problem.
- Write down what you confirmed and what is still unknown.
Words to know:
- Country Commercial Guide: a U.S. government report on how business works in a foreign country.
- Business registry: the official government office where companies and business names are registered.
- Market research: finding out who your customers are, what they need and what they will pay.
Official sources:
- International Trade Administration: Country Commercial Guides
- International Trade Administration: Export solutions (U.S. Commercial Service)
- Kenya Business Registration Service
- Nigeria Corporate Affairs Commission
Try it now: Ask an AI assistant for the ten questions you must answer before starting your idea. Then open the Country Commercial Guide for your country on trade.gov and answer two of them from it.
You can now plan market research with AI and check key facts in official guides and registries.

check.q: What is a Country Commercial Guide?
options: A guide written by an AI
An official guide to doing business in a country, from the International Trade Administration
check.why: Country Commercial Guides are official market guides prepared by U.S. Embassy staff and published by the ITA.

check.q: The AI tells you the steps to register a company in Kenya. What do you do?
options: Check them with Kenya's Business Registration Service
check.why: Registration steps come from the country's own official registry.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Writing a one-page business model
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Write a one-page business model with AI help.
This lesson builds toward: Using your one-sentence idea, you will write a one-page business model with AI help, with all seven parts and every guess marked "to test".
A one-page business model answers the key questions on one page: Who is the customer? What problem do they have? What is your solution? Why you (your skills and edge)? How will you reach customers? How will you earn money? What are your main costs?
Give the AI your one-sentence idea and your notes, then ask: "Turn this into a one-page business model with these headings: customer, problem, solution, why me, channels, revenue, costs. Keep each to two or three lines."
Read it critically. If the AI says "farmers will gladly pay", ask yourself: did a farmer tell me that? Replace guesses with what you learned from real customers, and mark the rest as "to test".
Step by step:
- Give AI your one-sentence idea and research notes.
- Ask for a one-page model with customer, problem, solution, why me, channels, revenue and costs.
- Replace guesses with what real customers told you.
- Mark anything unproven as "to test".
Words to know:
- Business model: how a business creates value for customers and earns money.
- Revenue: money that comes in from customers.
- Channel: the way you reach and sell to customers.
Try it now: Ask an AI assistant to turn your one-sentence idea into a one-page business model with the seven headings. Mark every line that is a guess as "to test".
You can now write a one-page business model and separate facts from guesses.

check.q: In a business model, what is revenue?
options: Money that comes in from customers
check.why: Revenue is money coming in from customers.

check.q: Your model says customers will pay $20 a month, but nobody has told you that. What do you do?
options: Mark it "to test" and ask real customers
check.why: Guesses stay marked "to test" until real customers confirm them.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Planning for money, risk and the law
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: List your start-up costs, your top three risks and how you will reduce each.
This lesson builds toward: For your business model, you will list your start-up costs and your top three risks with one way to reduce each, with prices from real quotes and no plan that relies on a bribe.
List what you need to start: equipment, transport, space, registration and licenses, a local partner or staff, and enough money to run for several months before sales cover costs. Ask AI for a checklist, then get real prices locally. Do not trust AI price guesses.
Common risks: currency swings (your costs and prices in different currencies), unreliable power or transport, payment delays, partners who do not deliver, theft, and changing rules. For each, write how you will reduce it: for example, price in local currency with a review every quarter, a backup generator, or a written agreement.
Never pay a bribe. Beyond local laws, the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act makes it a crime for U.S. persons to offer or pay anything of value to a foreign official to win or keep business. For contracts, tax and registration, use a qualified local lawyer or accountant.
Step by step:
- Ask AI for a start-up cost checklist for your idea.
- Get real local prices for each item.
- List your top three risks.
- Write one way to reduce each risk.
- Note which questions need a local lawyer or accountant.
Words to know:
- Start-up costs: the money you need before the business earns enough to pay for itself.
- Bribe: something of value given to an official to get an unfair advantage; illegal.
- Foreign Corrupt Practices Act: a U.S. law that makes bribing foreign officials to get business a crime.
Official sources:
- U.S. Department of Justice: Foreign Corrupt Practices Act
Try it now: Ask an AI assistant for a start-up cost checklist for your idea. Then write your top three risks and one way to reduce each.
You can now plan start-up costs, name your top risks with fixes, and know the legal lines you must not cross.

check.why: Start-up costs include equipment, registration, staff and months of running costs.

check.q: A clerk says a small cash payment will speed up your license. What do you do?
options: Refuse, because bribery is illegal, including under the U.S. FCPA
check.why: Paying a foreign official for business is a crime under the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Testing the idea and getting official help
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Plan a small, cheap test of your idea and choose one official help program to contact.
This lesson builds toward: Before you spend real money, you will plan a small, cheap pilot of your idea and choose one official help program to contact, with the program named and a date to contact it.
Before you move abroad or spend your savings, test small. Run a pilot: serve ten customers, sell a small batch, or partner with one local business for a month. Track what customers pay, what it costs you and what goes wrong. AI can help you design a simple tracking sheet.
Free official help: the SBA's Boots to Business is an entrepreneurship course offered through the Transition Assistance Program for service members, National Guard, Reserve and military spouses; Boots to Business Reboot extends it to veterans of all eras. Veterans Business Outreach Centers offer workshops, mentoring and business plan help. The U.S. Commercial Service helps U.S. businesses that sell abroad.
Bring your one-page model to them. A mentor who has done business abroad can save you from expensive mistakes.
Step by step:
- Design a small pilot: how many customers, how long, what to measure.
- Ask AI to build a simple tracking sheet: sales, costs, problems.
- Pick one official help program.
- Contact it and bring your one-page model.
Words to know:
- Pilot: a small, short test of a business idea before you go all in.
- Boots to Business: a free SBA entrepreneurship course for service members, veterans and military spouses.
- Veterans Business Outreach Center: an SBA-supported center that gives veterans business training and mentoring.
Official sources:
- SBA: Boots to Business
- SBA: Veteran-owned businesses (VBOCs, Boots to Business Reboot)
- International Trade Administration: Export solutions
Try it now: Final task: finish your one-page business model with customer, problem, solution and military-skill fit, channels, revenue, costs and top three risks. Add a research plan naming the Country Commercial Guide, the country's business registry and one official help program you will contact.
You can now plan a small test of your business idea and get free official help to build it.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Customer, problem and fit The customer or problem is vague, or the military skill is not linked. A named customer, a real problem, a solution and how a military skill fits. The learner can say how they know the problem is real. Complete business model Channels, revenue or costs are missing. All seven parts on one page, with guesses marked "to test". Each "to test" line has a way to test it. Risks Fewer than three risks, or no way to reduce them. Top three risks, each with one way to reduce it, and no plan that relies on a bribe. Risks include currency and rules, with a named professional to ask. Research plan No official sources named. Names the Country Commercial Guide and the country's business registration agency. Shows two research questions already answered from those sources. Official help No help program named. One free official help program the learner will contact. Includes a date to contact it and a small pilot to run first. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

options: A small, short test of your idea
A full launch in every city
check.why: A pilot tests your idea cheaply before you spend real money.

check.q: You finished your one-page model. What official help do you add to your plan?
options: A paid seminar from an online ad
Boots to Business or another free official program
A stranger who promises fast profits
check.why: Free official programs like the SBA's Boots to Business teach veterans to start businesses.
